name: Azure MCP Server
outcome_statement: As of 2026-11-14: meets C2, C3, C4, C6, C8, C9, C10; partly meets C1, C5, C7.

findings.title: Source and release provenance
findings.finding: The npm record for @azure/mcp@4.0.0-beta.7 names the repository `git+https://github.com/microsoft/mcp.git`. The record carries no provenance attestation (`dist.attestations` is absent).

findings.title: Published security policy
findings.finding: GitHub shows a security policy for the repository (`SECURITY.md` in the repository), and it describes how to report a vulnerability.

findings.title: Maintenance status
findings.finding: The repository is not archived and the package is not marked deprecated. Latest release 4.0.0-beta.7 is dated 2026-11-11; the newest commit on `main` is dated 2026-11-14; GitHub reports the last push on 2026-11-14.

findings.title: Published advisories
findings.finding: No advisory is published in the repository's advisory list.

findings.title: Documented scope controls
findings.finding: Tools can create, modify and delete resources within the signed-in identity's Azure permissions; the security policy documents options that limit which tools are exposed and calls them operational guardrails, and the README advises least-privilege roles. Quoted: “MCP tools are designed to inspect, create, modify, and delete Azure resources”; “which MCP servers and tools are enabled (for example, via `--namespace`, `--tool`, `--mode`, `--read-only`, and `--disable-proxy-tools`)”; “You should review and apply least-privilege RBAC roles and implement safeguards before deployment.”.

findings.title: Credential handling in the documented setup
findings.finding: Credentials are handled through the Azure Identity SDK. Quoted: “we never store or manage tokens directly”.

findings.title: Telemetry and outbound data, as documented
findings.finding: Telemetry is documented as on by default, with an environment variable to turn it off. Quoted: “Telemetry collection is on by default.”; “set the environment variable `AZURE_MCP_COLLECT_TELEMETRY` to `false`”.

findings.title: Dependency management files
findings.finding: A lockfile (`Directory.Packages.props` (central package-version file)) and an update configuration (`.github/dependabot.yml`) are committed.

findings.title: Documentation of untrusted-content risk
findings.finding: The security policy names prompt injection and untrusted input, and states that callers and MCP hosts are responsible for inspecting and sanitising returned data. Quoted: “Reports involving AI-generated tool calls or prompt injection must demonstrate a violation of a security responsibility owned by the MCP server”; “It is the responsibility of callers, users, and MCP hosts to inspect, validate, and sanitize inputs and returned data before using them in ways that may impact their environment.”.

findings.title: Currency of the declared MCP library
findings.finding: Declared MCP library: ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0 in Directory.Packages.props. Lower-bound version 2.2.0 of ModelContextProtocol (NuGet) was published on 2026-08-13, within the 12 months before 2026-11-14.
